notes:
Account snapshot: VectorHaven builds product analytics tooling that enriches logs with embeddings + an interactive chat assistant for product teams. Mid-market SaaS with high-frequency inference and bursty e2e workflows (nightly batch + realtime chat). Current vendor: OpenAI (usage ~120M tokens/mo). Primary driver: predictable latency and price, plus VPC/Dedicated for data isolation for enterprise customers.

POC details / migration story:
- Team elected to run Hosted API POC first to validate functional parity and measure token economics before committing to Dedicated.
- Implemented a lightweight compatibility layer (shim) that translates existing OpenAI-style calls to Redwood endpoints to minimize app changes. Shim covers completions, chat, streaming and embeddings endpoints.
- Prompt parity checks: created a 500-prompt test-suite (ranking/summarization/chat) to compare outputs. Most prompts matched; ~0.6–0.9% of prompts produced notable semantic differences (date normalization, list ordering, and code-block formatting).
- Root-cause investigation: differences concentrated on a custom system prompt handling and a slightly different default temperature/top_p mapping. SE recommended explicit prompt scaffolding and pinned model version; also suggested Redwood Optimize quantization profile for embeddings.
- Performance: Hosted API p50 chat latency ~140ms (within target), p95 spikes to 420ms under burst tests; Dedicated expected to bring p95 <200ms with reserved capacity and smarter batching.
- Cost: Hosted run extrapolation showed higher variable spend at current volumes; Dedicated committed capacity expected to cut per-token spend substantially given their steady baseline.

Security & compliance:
- They require SSO (SAML) integration for admin console access, SOC2 attestation, KMS support for customer-managed keys, and the ability to keep audit logs in EU region for EU customers. Redwood security doc answered most items; they want a detailed diagram of the Private/Dedicated control plane and where logs are stored.

Operational concerns & requests:
- Need predictable fallback behavior during Dedicated rollout. They want an automated compat routing policy (hosted fallback) and a step-by-step DR runbook.
- Regression monitoring: want to integrate Redwood eval alerts in their CI to gate releases; ask for webhook for regression events.
- Prompt versioning: request SDK sample to pin system prompts and do prompt diffs.

Commercial/Procurement notes:
- Procurement asked for consumption vs. reserved sizing comparison. Finance is cost-sensitive — target is to get to 90%+ of current accuracy at <=75% of current spend per active user. Forecasting ARR: team expects 75k–250k ARR depending on committed Tiers.
- Legal flagged data residency clause (must ensure EU logs for EU tenant data and contract-limited retention).

Quotes/Direct feedback:
- Engineering lead Priya: "We want minimal code churn — the compat shim is working but we need strict prompt parity on critical reranking flows."
- Head of Product Tom: "If Redwood can guarantee p95 improvements and reduce unit costs, Dedicated is a no-brainer; but regressions during model swaps are our single biggest fear."

migration_notes: Compatibility approach: shim acts as drop-in replacement for OpenAI calls; kept param mapping explicit (temperature, top_p, stream). For function-calling parity we mapped JSON schema handling and validated 120 test calls. Regression categories: formatting, deterministic date parsing, and small hallucination cases. Suggested mitigations: pin model variant, explicit system msg, and add lightweight post-processing for sorting lists to match previous behavior.
risks:
